title: Linear equations and word problems: practice set
sourceNote: Original practice questions written for this group. None of them is a CAT previous-year question.
instructions: 10 questions, 20 minutes, CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

questions.text: A pen costs ₹5 more than a pencil. Three pens and two pencils together cost ₹65. What is the price of one pen?
The sum of three consecutive integers is 96. What is the largest of them?
A father is 4 times as old as his son. After 5 years he will be 3 times as old as his son. What is the son's age now, in years?
A bag holds 20 coins, all of ₹2 or ₹5. Their total value is ₹64. How many ₹5 coins are in the bag?
For which value of k does the system 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + ky = 14 have infinitely many solutions?
Solve x + 2y = 11 and 3x − y = 12. What is the value of x × y?
How many pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 3x + 5y = 47?
Ravi has only ₹10 notes and ₹50 notes. He has twice as many ₹10 notes as ₹50 notes, and the notes are worth ₹1,400 in total. How many notes does he have?
A fraction becomes 2/3 when 3 is added to both its numerator and its denominator. It becomes 1/2 when 2 is subtracted from both. What is the sum of the original numerator and denominator?
Ten years ago A was three times as old as B. Five years from now A will be twice as old as B. What is A's present age, in years?
